The canonical .claude/rules/instruction-files.md:9,27,37–47 defines `paths:` plus the no-key/every-session behavior. The surrounding README is current instructions, not a preserved command example.

Consequence: an auditor following the literal key can select the wrong instructions or omit applicable ones. Self-refutation: the canonical guide remains reachable, limiting severity; historical #314 methodology explains provenance but does not govern current rules. T39’s retained46 outcome routes and bounded issue searches assign no existing correction for this key. Source unchanged; no Phase7 outcome chosen.

Already written: documentation has not written device/cloud state; no user-data migration is implicated. Historical receipts and author identities must remain byte-exact.

Can this be done on the VM? Documentary source comparison and current rule checks need no runtime; no device fact or guest behavior is claimed.

Acceptance: a separately authorized current-doc correction names the actual `paths:` convention and every-session behavior, with a bounded source trace and rules/record checks showing the wording agrees with instruction-files.md. Exact changed-path evidence must show historical receipts untouched. Root owns that stream disposition; this audit does not apply the correction.

Evidence: 02-forward-audit.md L-01, stage-b/table.json finding_trace, stage-b/read-00/stdout, stage-b/inherited-and-duplicates.json. Reactive issue assigned in Stage D summary/readback.

bug.body:
Discovered by T46 #693, Local actual primary Codex / GPT-6-Astra / xhigh, T3 wN:p6. Severity Low; Documentation Gap. Source reviewed-at d707c82ab8c48b674acc1f95a9571f0cb24d226a. No fix applied; root retains stream disposition. This reactive bug has no milestone or parent.

## Literal trace and reader consequence

At that source, docs/audits/README.md:19 instructs auditors to use instruction files whose `applyTo` matches changed paths. The current canonical .claude/rules/instruction-files.md:9,27,37–47 specifies `paths:`, including omitted-key/every-session behavior. The README’s surrounding lines17–22 describe current audit practice. A literal reader can search for the wrong selector and omit applicable rules.

README SHA25617269ce0820878e809890a9f737cd665c77d32ff07a20e779aed4fac1b745d79; instruction guide SHA256ca638c32b6bbf991c02a865b9c3ab19279416806e7baa0a320713989610da845. Evidence: docs/audits/2026_11_03-epic-m6-records/02-forward-audit.md, stage-b/table.json finding_trace and stage-b/read-00/stdout in feature/m6-records-693.

## Self-refutation and existing owners

The canonical guide remains reachable, so this is Low documentary risk, not an observed runtime failure. Historical #314 comment5879416677 preserves old Copilot methodology; that explains provenance but does not make this current instruction correct. The accepted T39 46-outcome bridge contains no correction for this key; its README release instruction correction is separate PL-02/#1400. Targeted searches for applyTo and docs/audits/README.md returned only #314 and #693 respectively. Search scope is retained, not claimed exhaustive.

Already written: this documentation wrote no device/cloud state; no user-data migration is implicated. Historical receipts and author identities must remain unchanged.

Can this be done on the VM? Documentary source comparison and current rule/record checks need no runtime. No device or guest behavior is claimed.

- [ ] A bounded committed source trace shows the current audit README names the actual `paths:` convention and every-session behavior consistently with instruction-files.md.
- [ ] The correction’s rules/record checks pass, and its exact changed-path evidence proves historical receipts and source programs unchanged.

No source correction, Phase7 resolution or closure is authorized by this issue alone; T46 stops at D for root disposition.
